linen.usage: Page, menu and wall background. The default ground for everything.

canvas.usage: The website page ground: plain white in Linen, the evening brown in Evening. Linen stays the ground for print, signs and photo placeholders.

paper.usage: Raised panels on linen: cards, menu panels, the inside of a stamp.

kraft.usage: Paper bags, hang tags and cup sleeves. Text on kraft is espresso or ink-muted; rust and sage-ink only at 24px and larger.

line.usage: Hairlines and card borders. Decorative only, never the only thing that separates two states.

espresso.usage: Main text and the logo, on linen, paper and kraft in both themes.

ink-muted.usage: Secondary text, notes and captions, on linen, paper and kraft.

rust.usage: The Kuha Ko Coffee accent: prices, sale marks, links, the grave accent in the logo. As text on linen and paper; as a fill under on-rust text.

on-rust.usage: Text and marks on a rust fill.

sage.usage: Decorative fills only: plants, the Kuha Ko Thrift block, cover shapes. Never small text.

sage-ink.usage: The Kuha Ko Thrift accent as text, on linen and paper; on kraft at 24px and larger.

mustard.usage: Highlights on board only: the live-selling claim, lamp-light details. Never text on linen.

board.usage: Dark panels: the shop sign, menu board, live-selling banner. Text on it is on-board or mustard.

focus-ring.usage: Keyboard focus on any screen: a solid 2px ring with a 2px gap in the ground colour. Meets 3:1 on linen, paper and board.

display.purpose: The hero line only; the second line in italic 400, rust.

headline.purpose: Page and section titles, sentence case.

title.purpose: Menu item names, card, panel and sheet titles.

body.purpose: Descriptions and running text; ledes at 18px, 40 to 52ch.

small.purpose: Notes and fine print; the smallest reading size.

label.purpose: Capitals with 3px tracking: section labels, nav, stamps.

tag.purpose: Hang tags, prices, item numbers, receipts.

themes.name: Evening (dark)
themes.note: Every colour token swaps to its dark value; see colorMeta.<name>.dark.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The site's easing for surfaces, slides, reveals and hovers.

motion.name: duration-stagger
motion.purpose: Per item in a staggered list.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover in, dropdown open, tabs, icon swaps, toast close.

motion.name: duration-medium
motion.purpose: Hover out, panel close, toast open.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Feedback on press for every button.

motion.name: sheet-spring
motion.value: spring: damping 0.85 to 1, response 0.32s, carries release velocity
motion.purpose: Dragging and dismissing the bottom sheet (src/motion.ts).

motion.name: hang-swing
motion.purpose: Rack pieces and price tags swinging when touched.

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.note: The sheet becomes a right-hand drawer on the full site from here up.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Tagged Rack"**

The site is a well-kept rack in a small shop: plain white walls, a hairline rail, and on it one piece at a time, each with a kraft tag that tells you the truth about it. Fraunces is the painted sign above the rack, Courier Prime is the typewriter that fills in the tags and the receipts, and DM Sans is the friend behind the counter explaining things in plain words. The coffee side and the thrift side hang on the same rail; colour tells them apart (rust for coffee, sage-ink for thrift) only where a customer needs to know which is which.

Density is low and the pace is unhurried. Sections breathe (80 to 152px of space between them), headings are large, and lists read like menus and tag cards rather than dashboards. Depth comes from paper, not light: linen and paper panels, hairline rules and the occasional dark sign board. Nothing floats on a shadow.

The interface is warm and playful in its details. Things that hang react when a hand reaches them: rack pieces and price tags swing, a stamp thunks onto a claimed item, the basket nods, the receipt prints, the lamp chain switches the evening theme. Motion that answers a touch is welcome; motion that plays on its own is rationed to a few signature moments (the hero's entrance, the rack's pieces sliding along the rail). The photography rule is the same as the tag rule: real drinks and real pieces in daylight, nothing staged or generated.
keyCharacteristics: White canvas, linen and paper bands, one dark board per page at most.
Square corners everywhere except the hang tag, which is the one rounded shape.
Serif signs, typewriter tags, sans body: three faces, each with one job.
Things that hang, swing; things that are claimed, get stamped.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: A piece of the page belongs to one shop at a time: rust for coffee, sage-ink for thrift. The shared shop uses espresso alone, with rust only for prices. Never put both accents on the same component.

rules.name: The Board Rule
rules.body: Mustard lives only on board. If a highlight needs to appear on linen, canvas or paper, it is rust or sage-ink, never mustard.

rules.name: The Hairline Is Not a State Rule
rules.body: A line-coloured hairline decorates; it never alone tells two states apart. Selected, active and error states change text colour, weight or fill as well.

rules.name: The Capitals Are for Labels Rule
rules.body: Capitals appear only in the label style, the stamp and the claim word KUHA KO!. Headings, menu items and buttons are sentence case.

rules.name: The Typewriter Tells the Truth Rule
rules.body: Anything factual about an item (number, size, measurements, price, "One of one") is set in Courier Prime, like a tag filled in by hand at the counter.

rules.name: The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: Kúha Ko, with its acute accent, bold "Kúha" and light italic "Ko", exists only as logo artwork. In type and copy it is Kuha Ko.

rules.name: The Paper, Not Light Rule
rules.body: To lift something, change its paper (canvas to paper to kraft) or draw a hairline. Never add a box-shadow, glow or gradient.

rules.name: The One Round Shape Rule
rules.body: If it isn't a hang tag, a stamp or a status chip, its corners are 4px. Rounded cards and pill buttons don't belong here.

dos: Do keep corners at 4px (radius-sm) on every card, panel, button and field; save the 60px arc for hang tags.
Do separate with 1px hairlines and paper panels.
Do give each piece of the page one accent: rust for coffee, sage-ink for thrift, espresso for the shared shop.
Do set item facts (numbers, sizes, measurements, prices) in Courier Prime.
Do keep every text pair at 4.5:1 contrast in both Linen and Evening.
Do show press feedback on press (scale 0.97) and let hanging things swing when touched.
Do use real photos of the shop's own drinks and pieces in daylight; until they exist, show the photo placeholder with its shot brief.
Do use simple line icons (1.5px stroke, espresso) with a word next to them.
donts: Don't add drop shadows, glows or gradients.
Don't use mustard anywhere but on board, or sage as a text colour.
Don't set headings, buttons or menu items in capitals; capitals are for labels, the stamp and KUHA KO! only.
Don't use the accented Kúha outside the logo artwork.
Don't use emoji, stock photos or AI-made images of products the shop sells.
Don't hard-code colours; every colour comes from a token so the Evening theme works.
Don't fade and slide sections in as they scroll into view; keep entrance motion to the hero and the rack.
Don't append arrows to links or number things that aren't a sequence.
